records.summary: Build a searchable directory of online communities across platforms, with listings, niche information, member counts, reviews, and participation features. The proposed business would help people find communities and earn money from enhanced listings or subscriptions.
records.how_money: Paid enhanced listings or subscriptions; Hive Index also lists topic-page ads at $50/month. Revenue from these models is unverified.
records.customer: People looking for online communities and community operators seeking promotion.
records.market: Online communities across multiple platforms; no specific country is stated.

revenue_claims.claim: A 2022 interview reported Hive Index at roughly $500 MRR from sponsorships; founder-reported and unaudited.
Hive Index reports 5,857 communities across 36 platforms and 294 topics.
Hive Index offers Gold at $390/year and Featured at $99 for a one-time 30-day placement; its FAQ instead says Featured is $99/month.
Hive Index offers topic-page ads at $50/month.

records.paid_demand: A 2022 interview reported roughly $500 MRR from sponsorships, but this is old, founder-reported evidence and current revenue is unverified. Current listing and advertising prices are displayed, but sales and advertiser returns are unverified.

competitors.name: Hive Index
competitors.price: Free listings; Gold $390/year; Featured $99 for a one-time 30-day placement (FAQ says $99/month); topic-page ads $50/month
competitors.note: Established cross-platform directory with thousands of listings.

competitors.name: Circle Discover
competitors.note: Discovery for Circle-hosted communities; listing price unverified.

competitors.name: AI Tech Communities
competitors.note: Article describes a 200-community directory; launch date unverified.

rounds.plain: K0 means the moat score was under 4: a bare directory is easy to copy and Hive Index already has thousands of listings. K5 means the only dated revenue evidence was from 2022, over 18 months old.

The check found no verified recent broad-directory launch that decisively killed the idea. Hive Index already has structured listings and reviews, while Circle Discover covers Circle-hosted communities.

risks: Current revenue, paid-customer count, churn, and operator hours are unverified.
Featured placement pricing is inconsistent on Hive Index’s page.
Scraping and platform API use may be restricted; stale listings, review abuse, and search dependence are risks.
A new entrant would need original, regularly verified data to distinguish itself.
records.moat: A maintained, independently sourced cross-platform dataset with verified freshness and trustworthy reviews could compound over time. That advantage does not yet exist for a new entrant, and the bare directory is easy to copy.
records.next_steps: Choose one niche and use Google Keyword Planner to check location-specific search estimates, then inspect search results and Hive Index pages for a visible gap. Compare that niche with Hive Index’s topic traffic and promotion figures; this does not prove willingness to pay.

records.summary: Build a subscription benchmark and discovery service for paid-community operators and prospective members. It would compare community prices, sizes, niches, and changes over time.
records.how_money: Proposed subscription service; subscription pricing and revenue are unverified.
records.customer: Paid-community operators and prospective members; the sources also discuss researchers and operators tracking communities.
records.market: Online communities, including Skool communities; no specific country is stated.

revenue_claims.claim: Check the Course displayed 9,448 listings and 1,252,883 observations.
Skool’s Careers page claims 30M+ users, 200,000+ communities and over $1B paid out to creators; it gives no measurement date or methodology.

records.paid_demand: No customer payments or paid users for the proposed benchmark service are verified. Competitors show free reports and tools, while adjacent products display prices; those prices do not establish sales.

competitors.name: Check the Course
competitors.note: Tracks community prices and membership with history and reports.

competitors.name: CommunityRank
competitors.note: Publishes community rankings and reports.

competitors.name: Skool Analytics
competitors.note: Owner-side analytics, not a cross-market benchmark.

competitors.name: Skool Stats
competitors.price: $149/month for 200 email enrichments in an October 2026 pricing review
competitors.note: Adjacent lead intelligence, not a benchmark subscription.

competitors.name: Skoolgrades Pro
competitors.note: Owner-side analytics.

rounds.plain: K0 means the moat score was under 4: overlapping free trackers already exist, and a unique permissioned dataset is not evidenced.

The check found no verified dated launch or platform-wide bundled benchmark that decisively killed the idea. Skool’s native analytics covers an owner’s own community, while the proposed benchmark would compare across communities.

risks: No verified revenue, paid customers, churn, or willingness to pay for this service.
Skool terms prohibit scraping and commercial compilation of its displayed content; written permission or another authorized data source would be needed.
Existing free products overlap with the proposed service.
Public membership multiplied by list price can overstate actual earnings.
records.moat: Historical data could become useful, but overlapping free competitors already publish similar information. A stronger moat would require unique, permissioned longitudinal data such as verified paid membership, retention, or owner-submitted outcomes.

hours.note: No operating business or measured founder workload is evidenced.

records.next_steps: Create a one-page pilot offer for one narrow operator segment using only operator-submitted or otherwise authorized sample data. Measure paid pilot reservations separately from expressions of interest, using contextual search ads if needed.

records.summary: Build an API or subscription data product for researchers and operators tracking paid online communities. It would provide repeated observations of membership, prices, and niches, with sample-based benchmark reports.
records.how_money: Proposed subscription or API access; price and revenue are unverified.
records.customer: Researchers and operators tracking paid online communities.
records.market: Online communities, including Skool; no country is specified.

revenue_claims.claim: The site states 9,447 listings and 1,233,478 observations across 10 weeks.
On 23 Oct 2026, Check the Course reported 9,448 listings, 402,777 communities/products read in the last 28 days, and 1,252,883 readings across 10 weeks.
Skool Stats claims 121k+ communities; Playbuuk claims 71.9k+; these are vendor-reported coverage figures, not independent market counts.

records.paid_demand: No verified customer payments, revenue, or paid-user count were found. Competitor prices are offers, not proof of sales.

competitors.name: Check the Course
competitors.note: Publishes dated membership and price histories and benchmark reports.

competitors.name: Skool Analytics
competitors.note: Tracks community membership, prices, and activity.

competitors.note: Cross-community intelligence; price is not evidence of sales.

competitors.note: Scraper listing; actual launch date unverified.

competitors.name: Playbuuk
competitors.note: Claims 71.9k+ communities.

rounds.plain: K0 means the moat score was under 4. Existing trackers overlap with the idea, and lawful access to differentiated data is unproven.

The check found a compounding data asset in the existing tracker and no competitor launch with a verified date that decisively killed the idea. Skool has owner-side analytics, but no cross-community benchmark product was found in that check.

risks: No verified revenue, paid customers, churn, API sales, or willingness to pay.
Skool terms prohibit commercial compilation and automated scraping or monitoring; data access needs confirmed authorization or a permitted feed.
Several trackers already publish overlapping histories and benchmarks.
Public owner information can still be personal data and may require lawful handling.
records.moat: A source-linked longitudinal dataset could become useful, but history alone creates no network effect or switching cost. Defensibility depends on authorized access and differentiated coverage, accuracy, and retained history beyond existing trackers.

hours.note: Estimate for a stable, authorized, self-serve operation; initial source clearance and build would exceed that target.

records.next_steps: Make a sample report using only a source whose terms permit reuse, then present a paid-pilot offer on an inbound landing page. Count paid pilot checkouts rather than clicks or free signups; if authorized sample data is unavailable, test the concept without presenting fabricated figures.

records.summary: Build a searchable directory that matches people with online communities using member reviews, topic tags, and platform information. The proposed business would sell premium discovery and analytics to community operators.
records.how_money: Proposed premium discovery and analytics for community operators; sales and subscription revenue are unverified.
records.customer: People seeking online communities and community operators.
records.market: Communities across multiple platforms; no country is specified.

revenue_claims.claim: Hive Index reports 5,855 communities across 294 topics and 36 platforms.
Hive Index’s homepage displays “Sponsored this month by Altium”; fee, payment versus in-kind status, and transaction evidence are not public.

records.paid_demand: Hive Index displays a current sponsor claim, but the fee and whether it was paid or in-kind are unverified. Its published prices for placements and sponsorships show offers, not proof of sales.

competitors.name: Hive Index
competitors.price: Free basic listings; Featured $99 for 30 days; Gold $390/year; site sponsorship $1,000/month
competitors.note: Its FAQ contradicts the Featured price, describing it as $99/month.

competitors.name: Unita
competitors.price: Sponsorship at $1,000/month or $1,500/month for its full package
competitors.note: Claims 30,000 community seekers and owners visit monthly; self-reported.

competitors.name: Discordium
competitors.note: Discord-specific premium plans; several analytics features are marked as coming soon.

competitors.name: Community Stack Junction
competitors.note: Launched 2026-10-16 and includes a directory and cross-community discovery for technical communities.

competitors.name: OpenCommunity
competitors.note: Describes a 700+ community directory; product launch date unverified.

rounds.plain: K0 means the moat score was under 4. The proposed network effect and review dataset are not established, and Hive Index already has thousands of listings.
The check found no exact like-for-like new launch with a verified date. Hive Index and Unita already offer community discovery, while Hive Index also provides reviews and paid promotion.

risks: No verified revenue, churn, profit, or paid-customer count.
Many Hive Index topic pages show no active promotions, so paying-operator demand is not established by price lists.
Featured listing pricing is inconsistent.
Scraping or reusing Hive Index, Reddit, or Discord data is constrained by published terms.
Review abuse and fake reviews create trust and compliance risks.
records.moat: A maintained, permissioned dataset of owner-submitted listings, freshness checks, and genuine reviews could create a data and network advantage. The concept does not yet establish that advantage, and basic directories and tags are easy to copy.

hours.note: Post-launch design target only if listings are self-submitted, billing is self-serve, and agents handle routine checks; actual hours are unverified.

records.next_steps: Choose one niche, publish a small page with owner-submitted listings and a review prompt, and test a clearly disclosed Featured offer using Hive Index’s stated one-time $99 for 30 days. Track seeker signups, owner submissions, and actual paid reservations; do not copy Hive Index’s dataset.
